clue.text: Wildly happy and glorious'? Not half — this shows it's a lie

indicators.note: wildly says the letters that follow are thrown about into a new order
not half tells us to keep only the front half of the word glorious and lose the rest

explanation.surface: A jab at the anthem line 'happy and glorious', saying only half of it is true and the rest a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps GLOR, the first half of 'glorious'; 'Wildly' rearranges HAPPY plus GLOR. The quote mark points to the British national anthem's line 'happy and glorious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector is a machine recording pulse and breathing to reveal when someone is not telling the truth.

clue.text: Former source of mutton's one supplying meat

parts.note: former means past, from before
mutton comes from a sheep, and a ram is a male sheep
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something about a sheep that once gave mutton now providing meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a highly seasoned smoked beef, a kind of cured meat.

clue.text: Angry? As it happens, receiving cut, I deserted

indicators.note: cut tells us to clip a letter off the end of the broadcast word

parts.note: something broadcast as it happens is live
D is the abbreviation for deserted, as in old service records

explanation.surface: Someone furious at being left out of a share when it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving cut' means LIVE is given a cut, losing its last letter to leave LIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is an informal word for furious, very cross.

clue.text: Booze barman wrongly associated with greed -it's for sweet tooth

parts.note: gin is a kind of booze, a spirit

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters of the words named are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A barman who drinks and is linked with greed, apparently it's all down to having a sweet tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' just joins the two words to be rearranged; 'it's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingerbread man is a biscuit shaped like a person, a treat for someone who loves sugary things.

clue.text: Clothing — paper slacks-carried by man

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the name that follows

parts.note: Al is a man's name, short for Alan or Albert

indicators.note: slacks, read as a verb, suggests the letters loosen up and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Clothing talk: a paper about trousers carried around by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slacks' looks like the trousers, which suits 'Clothing', but here it is a verb telling the paper's letters to loosen into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments, what someone wears.

clue.text: Insect? Jinx on a part of pea plant

parts.note: a hex is a curse, a jinx
the pod is the case that holds peas

explanation.surface: A bug that puts a curse on part of a pea plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexapod means six-footed, and insects are the creatures with six legs.

clue.text: Society to cry about leader

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for cry is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Members of a club weeping over the person who runs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run of society plus cry backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person in charge, the head of an organisation.

clue.text: Going off on a bender?

parts.note: milk that is going off is starting to sour; a bender is also a bend in the road, so someone on it is rounding a curve

explanation.surface: Someone setting out on a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests leaving for a boozy spree; the answer says both 'starting to sour' and 'midway round a bend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food on the turn is beginning to spoil, and a car on the turn is going round a corner.

clue.text: Calm and a little eased at Evensong

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchgoer feeling calmer and somewhat soothed at the evening service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means quiet and composed, unhurried.

clue.text: Real bang? Trick'd come from this!

definitions.text: Real bang? Trick'd come from this!

indicators.note: come from says the answer's letters can be made from the words before, rearranged

explanation.surface: A trick done with a fake shot that makes a real-sounding bang.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a blank makes a bang with no bullet, so the bang seems real but is a trick, and its letters come from REAL BANG TRICKD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank cartridge holds powder but no bullet, so it gives a loud report without a shot.

clue.text: End of this is not odd? This is odd

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a number that is not odd is even

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether something is odd or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of this' gives S; the second 'This' is the definition, a number that is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is an odd number, not divisible by two.

clue.text: One leading football team in trophy's dead drunk

indicators.note: in places the one-plus-team pair inside the trophy word

parts.note: a plate is a trophy, as in a racing plate

indicators.note: leading says one comes in front of the football team

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
D is an abbreviation for dead, as in family records

explanation.surface: A footballer who led his side to a cup is now completely sloshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixilated is a slang term for tipsy, also meaning a bit dotty.

clue.text: Creature studied at great expense we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: studied is read, and at great expense is dear, so the phrase sounds like read dear

explanation.surface: A creature that someone researched at enormous cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large animal found in Britain's moors and forests.

clue.text: Smelly dirt, perhaps, in boat

indicators.note: in places the information word inside the boat word

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat
dirt on someone is information, and gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Something smelly, maybe dirty water, found in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means having a strong, sharp odour.

clue.text: Claim I bruited abroad, wonderful to relate

indicators.note: abroad, meaning scattered far and wide, tells us the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims they spread a story far and wide, a marvel to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bruited' means spread about as rumour, which suits the surface story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is literally translated as a marvel to tell, said of an astonishing fact.

clue.text: Hungry King, able to eat a horse, say (with head removed)

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: with head removed means losing the first letter

parts.words: able to eat a horse, say
parts.note: someone able to eat a horse has a roomy appetite, so capacious

explanation.surface: A ravenous monarch who could devour a whole horse, minus its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means greedy and grasping, ravenous.

clue.text: Officer's agents mistakenly holding soldiers up

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: holding means one set of letters is gripped inside the other
mistakenly says the letters of the word before are put in the wrong order
up, in a down clue, means the soldiers' letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An officer's spies wrongly keeping the troops waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the soldiers' letters from the bottom; the scrambled agents, signalled by 'mistakenly', hold them around the third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or police.

clue.text: English consider getting involved in caper, for the most part

indicators.note: getting involved in puts the English-plus-consider pair inside the caper word

parts.note: to caper is to prance, leaping about
to ponder is to consider

explanation.surface: An Englishman thinks about joining a frolic, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: A preponderance is the greater share, the bulk of something.

clue.text: Dance round home, putting record on

parts.note: O is round in shape
a nest is a home, especially a bird's
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dance around the house while putting a record on.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance popular early in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Help to restrain anger in rising states of madness

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the whole assembled word is read upwards
to restrain means to hold the anger word inside the help word

parts.note: aid means help
to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: Assistance holding back fury in states of mounting madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' applies to the whole container built by 'to restrain', since in a down entry reading upwards reverses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliria is the plural of delirium, a disturbed mental state with confusion and raving.

clue.text: Plan something done in response

indicators.note: in puts the deed word inside the response word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch, a reflex response
an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: A plan devised in reaction to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a scheme or manoeuvre for gaining an end.

clue.text: Sense of apathy, one enveloping police inspector, initially

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapped around the police letters

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of inspector

explanation.surface: A bored feeling settling on one police inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidie is spiritual sloth, a listless indifference.

clue.text: Lying in wait, acting as bait to capture King

indicators.note: to capture means to hold the king letter inside

parts.note: something acting as bait is luring
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: Someone lying in wait with bait set out to capture a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurking means hiding nearby, waiting to ambush.

clue.text: Religion is a source of light, mostly

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the light word is dropped

parts.note: a lamp is a source of light

explanation.surface: Faith described as a light-giver, or nearly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith revealed through Muhammad.

clue.text: Ship? Anything from Yorkshire backed by captain

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect, used in Yorkshire, for anything
a ship's master is its captain

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire item supported by a ship's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns OWT into TWO; 'by' places it beside MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-master is a sailing vessel with two masts.

clue.text: Letter found in model tank

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: A letter discovered inside a toy tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Ape martyr unrolling such an aid to devotion

indicators.note: unrolling suggests the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey and a saint unrolling a mat for prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrolling' fits the definition: a prayer mat is rolled out before use.
